text: What pisses me off is the discourse around how women only go for the top 15% of men. Like, am I supposed to be going for the fat loser who doesn't have a job and lives at home? Am I supposed to be attracted to that? Obviously, I'm going to be attracted to the guy who's ambitious, the guy who's manly, the guy who takes care of himself and his health and works out, the guy who's tall, the guy who's going to give my kids good genetics. Why on earth would I be attracted to the fat loser? Or any loser, for that matter. Even an average guy. Like, if I could pick the best of the best, why would I be attracted to the mid-tier? Like, hello. Especially if I'm a top quality girl. So, in a way, she's saying that women only wanting the top 15% of men is just a common sense. Because why would she go for a fat loser without a job? Okay, let's break this down. First of all, yes, of course women are attracted to ambition, fitness, confidence, success. That's hypergamy. And it's been around forever. Women want to date upwards. Nothing new there. But here's the part she conveniently skips. If every woman only aims for the top 15%, what happens to the other 85% of men? They don't just disappear. They're still out there. And the problem is, when women collectively ignore average men, they create a dating market where a tiny group of guys have endless options. And the majority of men are invisible. That's why so many women end up frustrated too. Because those top guys don't settle. Now, I'll give her credit on one point. If you're a man, sitting at home doing nothing, you can't expect women to want you. You've got to build yourself up. Work on your body, your career, your confidence. Complaining won't help. But here's the reality check for women. Not every man is going to be top 15%. And if you think you are top quality, be prepared that those men also have standards. And you're competing with a lot of other women. So guys, don't play the victim. Build yourself up. And ladies, don't act like dating only the top 15% doesn't come with its own problems. Because it does.
